questions.knowledge_point: Stating the Vertex of a Vertical Parabola Given Its Equation in Standard Form
questions.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola ${x}^{2}=-y?$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at the origin is

$$
{x}^{2}=4py,
$$

where $p$ is a constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as 

$$
{x}^{2}=4(-\frac{1}{4})y.
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=-\frac{1}{4}.$ Therefore, our parabola has its vertex at $(0,0).$

questions.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $(x-2)^{2}=12(y+1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

where $p$ is constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2} & =4(3)(y+1).\end{aligned}
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=3.$

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have $h=2$ and $k=-1.$ Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are $(2,-1).$

questions.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $(y+6)^{2}=-6(x+8)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),
$$

where $p$ is constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as 

$$
(y+6)^{2}=4(-\frac{6}{4})(x+8),
$$

which simplifies to

$$
(y+6)^{2}=4(-\frac{3}{2})(x+8).
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=-\frac{3}{2}.$ 

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have $h=-8$ and $k=-6.$ Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are $(-8,-6).$

(x-h)^2 = 4p(y-k),

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =4(2)(y-2).\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $(y-2)^2=2(x+1)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(y-k)^2 = 4p(x-h),
$$

where $p$ is a constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as 

$$
(y-2)^2 = 4\left(\dfrac{2}{4}\right)(x +1),
$$

which simplifies to

$$
(y-2)^2 = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(x +1),
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=\dfrac{1}{2}.$ 

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have $h=-1$ and $k=2.$ Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are $\left(-1,2\right).$
